\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گیت} (git)}{گیت (git)}]{\fa{گیت} (git) — a gate (at an airport)}

\label{lesson:FA-C432-git}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an airline, then the Persian for a boarding pass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گیت}}
\textbf{\fa{گیت}} (\emph{git}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gate (at an airport)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مسافران} \fa{جلوی} \fa{گیت} \fa{شماره} \fa{پنج} \fa{صف} \fa{کشیدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mosâferân jolow-ye git-e shomâre-ye panj saf keshidand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The passengers queued in front of gate number five.
\end{quote}

Also the security gate you walk through.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{git} was borrowed from English and is usually traced to English \emph{gate}. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{git}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{git}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{git}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an airline, then the Persian for a boarding pass, then say \emph{git} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گذرنامه} (gozarnâme)}{گذرنامه (gozarnâme)}]{\fa{گذرنامه} (gozarnâme) — a passport (formal word)}

\label{lesson:FA-C432-gozarname}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a boarding pass, then the Persian for a gate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گذرنامه}}
\textbf{\fa{گذرنامه}} (\emph{gozarnâme}) — \textquotedblleft{}a passport (formal word)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مامور} \fa{فرودگاه} \fa{گذرنامه} \fa{من} \fa{را} \fa{نگاه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ma'mur-e forudgâh gozarnâme-ye man râ negâh kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The airport officer looked at my passport.
\end{quote}

The formal word; in speech \emph{pâsport} is more common. \emph{gozar} 'passing' + \emph{nâme} 'letter'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gozarnâme} is a native compound, a letter for passing: \emph{gozar} is the present stem of \emph{gozashtan} 'to pass', which EtymDB traces to a Middle Persian verb 'to pass, to cross', and \emph{nâme} 'letter' is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{nāmag}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gozarnâme}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gozarnâme}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gozarnâme}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a boarding pass, then the Persian for a gate, then say \emph{gozarnâme} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اضافه} \fa{بار} (ezâfe-bâr)}{اضافه بار (ezâfe-bâr)}]{\fa{اضافه} \fa{بار} (ezâfe-bâr) — excess baggage}

\label{lesson:FA-C432-ezafe-bar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a gate, then the Persian for a passport.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اضافه} \fa{بار}}
\textbf{\fa{اضافه} \fa{بار}} (\emph{ezâfe-bâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}excess baggage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{چمدان} \fa{من} \fa{سنگین} \fa{بود} \fa{و} \fa{اضافه} \fa{بار} \fa{دادم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Chamedân-e man sangin bud va ezâfe-bâr dâdam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My suitcase was heavy and I paid for excess baggage.
\end{quote}

\emph{ezâfe} 'extra' + \emph{bâr} 'load, luggage'. \emph{Ezâfe-bâr dâdan} — to pay for excess baggage.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ezâfe-bâr} is built from \emph{ezâfe} 'extra', borrowed from Arabic \emph{iḍāfa} 'adding, an adjunct' (EtymDB), and native \emph{bâr} 'load, burden', which EtymDB lists.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ezâfe-bâr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ezâfe-bâr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ezâfe-bâr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a gate, then the Persian for a passport, then say \emph{ezâfe-bâr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بازرسی} \fa{کردن} (bâzrasi kardan)}{بازرسی کردن (bâzrasi kardan)}]{\fa{بازرسی} \fa{کردن} (bâzrasi kardan) — to search, to inspect (bags or people)}

\label{lesson:FA-C432-bazrasi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a passport, then the Persian for excess baggage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بازرسی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بازرسی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{bâzrasi kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to search, to inspect (bags or people)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{فرودگاه} \fa{کیف} \fa{مرا} \fa{بازرسی} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar forudgâh kif-e marâ bâzrasi kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the airport they searched my bag.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâzrasi} 'inspection' + \emph{kardan}. An inspector is a \emph{bâzras}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâzrasi kardan} is built from native \emph{bâzrasi} 'inspection', from \emph{bâz} 'again, back' and \emph{ras}, the stem of \emph{residan} 'to reach', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâzrasi kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâzrasi kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâzrasi kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a passport, then the Persian for excess baggage, then say \emph{bâzrasi kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مهماندار} (mehmândâr)}{مهماندار (mehmândâr)}]{\fa{مهماندار} (mehmândâr) — a flight attendant; a host}

\label{lesson:FA-C432-mehmandar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for excess baggage, then the Persian for to search.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مهماندار}}
\textbf{\fa{مهماندار}} (\emph{mehmândâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a flight attendant; a host\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مهماندار} \fa{به} \fa{ما} \fa{آب} \fa{و} \fa{چای} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mehmândâr be mâ âb va chây dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flight attendant gave us water and tea.
\end{quote}

\emph{mehmân} 'guest' + \emph{dâr} 'keeper'. On a plane it is the cabin crew.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mehmândâr} is a native compound of \emph{mehmân} 'guest' and \emph{dâr} 'holder, keeper', from the stem of \emph{dâshtan} 'to have, to hold'. EtymDB lists the compound without older forms.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
